Tiszabezded Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tiszabezdéd, Hungary

Not demolished. Tiszabezdéd's Jewish cemetery, in use from 1853 to at least 1941, served a community first recorded in 1747 on the estates of four noble families. Jewish population peaked at 169 (43 households) in 1848, declining to 66 by 1941. Despite their small numbers, Jews had outsized local economic influence, including ownership of one of Hungary's largest Reform-Era distilleries. The community was nominally under Mándok's rabbinate but more strongly influenced by Kisvárda's. Anti-Jewish violence escalated in 1938 - the synagogue (built 1900) was desecrated, property destroyed, and one family unable to prove citizenship was deported to Kamianets-Podilskyi. In April 1944, the community was forced to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz by month's end; only 10 young survivors returned, leaving soon after to find the synagogue damaged (it was later torn down). By 1949, just 3 Jews remained.
